analysis:
MARKET REGIME: SPY uptrend is intact (+1.1% vs SMA50, slope +2.49%), which is constructive but not a reason to force deployment. The regime warrants staying invested in quality names but does not demand adding to an already full book.

PORTFOLIO REVIEW — Six positions is already above the stated 3-5 concentrated target. The profit factor sits at 0.79 (below 1.0) and the Sortino ratio is -1.64, both warning signs that selectivity has not been tight enough. The right response is higher quality filtering, not more activity.

CI (CIGNA) — most important flag: CI is down 5.07% from average cost, has healthcare managed care headwinds (Medicaid rate pressures, medical cost inflation), and critically it does NOT appear in today's screened candidate list. Absence from the screened list implies it may have a deteriorating trend signal. This is a thesis-break candidate. Watch the stop closely; if it violates a meaningful support level or the structural headwinds worsen, exit to protect capital. No averaging down.

LII — down 2.95%. A prior LII position was stopped out at -6.63%, then re-entered. The current position is inside normal ATR noise; thesis (HVAC replacement cycle, pricing power) is still intact for now. No action required but trail the stop.

A, FDS, WDAY, AMP — all in positive territory (+5-7%). FDS and WDAY are in the screened list as uptrend/basing setups, confirming thesis continuation. No reason to trim yet.

NEW CANDIDATES SCREEN: With 6 open positions, only $24K of headroom, and a negative profit factor, the bar for adding a 7th name is extremely high. The most interesting fundamentals belong to VEEV (PEG 0.87, FCF $1.3B, clean balance sheet) and ZBRA (PEG 0.55, fwd P/E 12.8). However: ZBRA reports in 18 days — binary event risk is unacceptable on a fresh entry. VEEV is 15.4% above its SMA50, which is extended for a new buy. CDW and DASH also report in 19 days. FICO, VLTO, VRSK, CBRE, and CMG all report within 12-13 days. AMAT is at 71% of its 52-week range, extended. DAL is at 84% of range — late-cycle entry. No candidate clears both the fundamental AND technical hurdles with acceptable earnings-event timing given the crowded book.

CONCLUSION: Cash is the correct position today. The portfolio already holds 6 names — above target — with a below-breakeven profit factor. Forcing a 7th position into a crowded, near-earnings landscape would compound the existing selectivity problem. Protect what is working, monitor CI for stop discipline, and wait for a clean setup with proper runway before next earnings season.
